reason: Locally correct (C=0 on every entry to .each: CLC;ADC #2 on widths <= &0B, and .next only after BNE on a non-zero ADC #0 result or an untaken BCS; SBC zp is 3 cycles either way, so the loop saves the CLC's 2 cycles and 1 byte). But the byte removed at &9740 slides every byte after it in DATA1 down by one, with no ALIGN before REN_BASE: the rest of the renderer (&9741-&A365), sprite_column_count, ck_index, the ck_* and straight_sprite tables and all the straight sprites (&A530-&B3xx). Scanning every branch in &9741-&A365: record_differs' first BNE out (listing &9FFE, D0 2E, next &A000 -> &A02E, same page) becomes &9FFD with next &9FFF -> &A02D, a page crossing: +1 cycle every time a record's type differs from its live slot (render.6502:446, called per shown record per pass). Indexed tables also move: ck_index &A3B2 (crossing from X>=&4E, becomes X>=&4F) and straight_sprite_hi &A4E4 (X>=&1C becomes X>=&1D) each lose one crossing index, and every straight sprite's data starts one byte lower, changing which rows/columns take draw_column's page-crossing paths (.on_same_page/.data_same_page/.save_same_page) in an uncounted direction. The candidate itself says the shift is not counted; the net per-pass effect (claimed 1.5 cycles) is therefore not established, and it has at least one concrete new cost. Not proven, so refuted; candidate 1's pairing with a +1-byte change (keeping the layout) is the safe form.
